applies_to: GS10 drives (built-in RS-485 port) per the GS10 user manual, 1st edition rev. C, chapter 5.
summary: The DURApulse GS10 is AutomationDirect's micro general-purpose drive with a built-in RS-485 Modbus RTU/ASCII port. Control goes through command words at 2000h-2002h and status is read from 2100h upward; every parameter Pxx.yy is also a register. This map covers the command and status words, frequency, voltages, the main serial setup parameters and the block-transfer registers.

addressing.note: Registers are listed in hex with the matching Modicon number (2000h = 48193, 2100h = 48449, 0900h = 42305). The hex value is the wire address; the manual's RTU examples send 21 02 to read 2102h and 20 00 to write 2000h.

source.title: DURApulse GS10 Drive User Manual - Chapter 5: Serial Communications
source.pages: communication parameters pp. 5-2 to 5-3; status and command addresses pp. 5-4 to 5-6; RTU examples pp. 5-13 to 5-14

notes: Parameter-to-register rule: Pxx.yy is at hex xx*256 + yy (P09.00 = 0900h = 42305; the block-transfer example P02.22 = 0216h). Only selected P09 communication parameters are listed; the rest are in chapter 4.
Values printed as XXX.XX carry two implied decimals (scale 0.01) and XXX.X one (scale 0.1).

Left out: output current (2104h), whose decimal places shift with the current and depend on 211Fh; output torque (210Bh), because its sign handling is not stated; P09.01 baud rate, P09.03 time-out and P09.09 response delay, whose raw encodings of decimal values are not given in this chapter.
Factory serial settings from the P09 summary: address 1, 38.4 kbps, protocol 13 (8 data bits, no parity, 2 stop bits, RTU).
Up to 12 words can be read in one request (function 03).

Control word 1 (2000h): bits 1-0 = 01 stop, 10 run, 11 jog + run; bits 5-4 = 01 forward, 10 reverse, 11 change direction; bits 7-6 accel/decel set; bits 11-8 multi-step speed; bit 12 enables bits 6-11; bits 14-13 = 01 keypad, 10 per P00.21, 11 change operation source.

integration.summary: Set the drive's run source and frequency source to RS-485, then write 2000h (run/stop/direction) and 2001h (frequency in 0.01 Hz) in one function-16 write. Poll 2100h-2106h for fault, state and frequency.
integration.enable: Set P09.00 address and P09.04 protocol (codes 12-17 are RTU), then select RS-485 as the frequency reference (P00.20 = 1 in Remote/Auto or P00.30 = 1 in Local/Hand, per the manual's note) and as the run-command source (see chapter 4).
integration.watchdog: P09.03 COM1 time-out detection (0.0-100.0 s, factory 0.0) sets the loss timeout; P09.02 selects warn, ramp-stop, coast-stop or no action on loss.
quirks: Hex addresses are the wire addresses.
If the RS-485 frequency reference exceeds P01.00, the drive runs at maximum output frequency.
setup: Use P09.04 to pick RTU framing (e.g. 13 = 8N2 RTU); all nodes must match.
gotchas: Block transfer registers P09.11-P09.26 let one read/write reach scattered parameters: write the target address (e.g. 8448 for 2100h) into a block-transfer slot.
Run command bits are a 2-bit code, not independent flags.
